I'll loop in Vivek (Solutions Engineering) for the technical deep dive. If you have any compliance docs you want us to review ahead of time, attach them or drop a link.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. Good summary. We're definitely interested in a sizing call.

Availability: Tue (Mar 23) or Wed (Mar 24) both look promising — prefer Tue morning if possible.

Preliminary sizing notes from our side (high level):
- Sustained baseline: ~50 requests/sec (RPS) for recommendation API calls
- Burst: up to 200 RPS for short windows (30–90s) during peaks
- Target tail: p95 <= 200ms for the user-facing endpoint; p99 is less critical but we'd like to understand tradeoffs
- Model: evaluating "gpt-open-8B" family for now; may explore larger variants if throughput/cost allow
- Average tokens: request ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens; typical seq len ~200

Who will join: myself (Product), Sasha (SRE), and I can loop in procurement if we need to discuss commercial terms.

Can you confirm if Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for recommendation flows and whether you have recommended batch sizes for the 8B family? Also curious about quantized model options to control cost.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Thanks for the context — I can run the sizing call next week. A few technical items I'd like to confirm ahead of the call to make the session productive:

- Target request size distribution (P10/P50/P90 token counts) and any long-tail "heavy" requests
- Typical sequence length and maximum allowed sequence length for generation
- Whether you expect multi-model routing (e.g., small model for most traffic, fallback to larger model)
- Acceptable cold-start window and whether KV/prefix caching is viable for your flows
- Burst characteristics: duration, frequency, and concurrent users during spikes

From a runtime perspective we'll cover:
- Batching strategies and recommended batch sizes for 8B-class models
- Quantization options (int8/4bit) with expected throughput improvements and any expected accuracy delta
- Autoscaling and dedicated GPU pool sizing for sustained vs burst workloads
- Observability hooks we'll use to validate performance post-deploy

If you can reply with the P90/P95 sequence lengths and a short CSV of traffic spikes, that would be ideal. Otherwise we'll treat the call as discovery and produce a follow-up sizing proposal.

I'll plan for a 60-minute slot. If Tue Mar 23 10:00 AM PT is confirmed, I'll prepare an initial capacity sketch and cost estimate.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
